construction_markdown:
No new code is claimed. I audit the following ordinary one-edge parity-lift template. Let `z_1,…,z_m` be binary vertex labels and let `G` be an undirected `D`-regular rotation multigraph, allowing integral loop and parallel-edge multiplicities. Every directed port from `u` to `v` is labeled `z_u+z_v`; the raw length is `M=mD`.

Let `H` be the span of these edge labels, with `h=dim(H)`. For each nonzero character `a∈H*`, put `W_a=Σ_i(-1)^{a(z_i+z_1)}` and let `ε=max_{a≠0}|W_a|/m`. If `λ` bounds every nontrivial absolute eigenvalue of the normalized adjacency matrix, the standard mixing certificate is

`β=ε²+λ(1−ε²)`.

The theorem below proves that this certificate, followed by generic zero padding or arbitrary fixed puncturing to length `2^30`, forces `h≤945`. Even adjoining one independent all-one row gives dimension at most 946.

I also audit uniformly repeated complete Cartesian XOR clouds: enumerate every ordered `t`-tuple of `m` seeds, label it by their XOR, and repeat every tuple equally often to obtain length `2^30`. For `t=2` the dimension is at most 785 after all-one augmentation; for `t≥3` it is at most 1025.

The proof combines the port-trace inequality with a 210th Fourier-moment count; thus this ordinary one-edge certificate cannot approach the proved `k=1040` endpoint.

explicitness_audit: This is a deterministic obstruction; no graph, seed set, or generator matrix is selected by search.
The port-trace argument permits loops and parallel edges with integral rotation-map multiplicities.
All numerical cutoffs use exact integer inequalities; no asymptotic constants or numerical optimization are invoked.
The one-edge result covers only the standard absolute base-bias/eigenvalue certificate and generic padding or puncturing. It does not exclude a direct code-specific one-sided correlation proof.
The Cartesian corollary covers complete tuple enumeration with uniform repetition. Sparse, unequal, or non-Cartesian path families remain outside its scope.

Uniformly repeated complete Cartesian XOR powers of every arity `t≥2` have dimension at most 1025, and the square case has the sharper ceiling 785.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem

Let `z_1,…,z_m` label the vertices of an undirected `D`-regular rotation multigraph. Form the raw binary character code from all `M=mD` directed ports, labeling a port from `u` to `v` by `z_u+z_v`. Suppose its distance after generic padding or puncturing to `n=2^30` is certified only through

`β=ε²+λ(1−ε²)`,

where `ε` is the maximum absolute bias of the translated vertex-label character code and `λ` is an absolute bound on every nontrivial eigenvalue of the normalized adjacency matrix. Then the raw homogeneous edge-label span has dimension at most 945. Puncturing cannot increase this dimension, and adjoining a single independent all-one row gives dimension at most 946.

### 1. Span and the standard edge certificate

Let `P` be normalized adjacency. A certificate capable of reaching the target has `λ<1`, so the graph is connected. Put `e_i=z_i+z_1`. Every edge label is `e_u+e_v`, while summing edge labels along a path from vertex 1 to vertex `i` gives `e_i`. Thus the edge-label span is exactly

`H=span{e_1,…,e_m}`.

Write `h=dim(H)`. For `a∈H*`, let `x_i=(-1)^{a(e_i)}`, `μ_a=m^{-1}Σ_i x_i`, and `ε=max_{a≠0}|μ_a|`. Decomposing `x=μ_a 1+y` with `y⊥1` gives

`|(1/m)x^T P x|≤μ_a²+λ(1−μ_a²)≤ε²+λ(1−ε²)=β`.

This is the standard complete directed-edge mixing certificate.

### 2. Length adjustment and trace force `m≤34,999`

Let `T=n−2D_target=2^21`. Padding a raw word with zeros adds `n−M` to its signed sum. Deleting `M−n` uncontrolled coordinates can increase its signed sum by at most `M−n`. Hence generic adjustment can certify the target only if

`βM+|n−M|≤T`.  (1)

It follows that `M∈[n−T,n+T]` and

`β≤T/(n−T)=1/511`.  (2)

In particular `λ≤1/511` and `ε²≤1/511`.

Write the integral adjacency multiplicities as `a_uv`. Symmetry and `a_uv²≥a_uv` give

`tr(P²)=Σ_{u,v}a_uv²/D²≥m/D`.

On the other hand, spectral decomposition and (2) give

`tr(P²)≤1+(m−1)/511²`.

With `q=511²=261121`, this yields

`qm≤D(q+m−1)`.

Since `mD=M≤n+T`,

`qm²≤(n+T)(q+m−1)`.  (3)

At `m=35000`, the left and right sides of (3) are respectively

`319,873,225,000,000` and `318,577,437,573,120`.

The difference function has positive derivative from this point onward because

`2q·35000−(n+T)=17,202,631,024>0`.

Therefore (3) forces `m≤34999`.

### 3. A 210th-moment rank bound

If `m<105`, then `h≤m−1≤103`. Assume `105≤m≤34999`. For every `a∈H*`, put

`W_a=Σ_i(-1)^{a(e_i)}`.

By (2), every nonprincipal character satisfies

`W_a^210≤(m²/511)^105=:A`.

Let `Z` count ordered 210-tuples of indices whose corresponding `e_i` values XOR to zero. Fourier orthogonality gives

`2^h Z=Σ_{a∈H*}W_a^210≤m^210+(2^h−1)A`,

and therefore

`2^h(Z−A)<m^210`.  (4)

Count only tuples obtained by selecting 105 distinct indices and using each twice. With `P=(209)!!`,

`Z≥(m)_105 P≥(m−104)^105P`.  (5)

We need only the elementary estimate `P>70^105`. Indeed,

`P=105!·binom(210,105)/2^105`.

The largest binomial coefficient is at least the average, so `binom(210,105)≥2^210/211`. Also integration of `log x` gives `105!≥e(105/e)^105`. The series for `e` gives `e<11/4`, hence

`P>(840/11)^105/211`.

Since `(12/11)^8>2`, one has `(12/11)^105>211`, proving `P>70^105`.

For `105≤m≤34999`, elementary differentiation reduces the extrema of `(m−104)/m²` to the endpoints. At the larger endpoint,

`100·70·511·34895=124819415000>123717930101=101·34999²`.

Thus (5) implies

`Z/A>[101/100]^105>2`,

where the last inequality already follows from the first three terms of the binomial expansion. Consequently `Z−A>Z/2`. Substituting in (4) gives

`2^h<2[m²/(70(m−104))]^105`.

The function `m²/(m−104)` again has its maximum at an endpoint. The endpoint checks are

`105²<512·70` and

`34999²=1224930001<1250636800=512·70·34895`.

Therefore

`2^h<2·512^105=2^946`,

so `h≤945`. An additional all-one direction raises dimension by at most one, proving the ceiling 946.

### 4. Complete Cartesian parity powers

Let `m` seeds generate every ordered `t`-tuple XOR, and repeat every tuple exactly `R` times, with `Rm^t=2^30`. If `t≥3`, then `m^t≤2^30`, so `m≤1024`. The tuple labels lie in the span of the seeds, giving homogeneous dimension at most 1024 and dimension at most 1025 after one constant direction.

For `t=2`, integrality of `R=2^30/m²` makes `m` a power of two with `m≤32768`. Repeat each seed `32768/m` times. The complete square of this enlarged 32,768-seed multiset repeats every original ordered pair exactly `R` times. It is therefore the same code up to coordinate order. The proved complete-square moment lemma gives homogeneous dimension at most 784 and all-one-augmented dimension at most 785.

Both audited complete-cloud templates are thus strictly below the current dimension-1040 endpoint. The proof does not address sparse path sets or direct one-sided cancellations.

proof_steps.proof: For raw length `M`, padding contributes `n−M` positive signs and arbitrary puncturing can increase the signed sum by at most `M−n`. Thus generic certification requires `βM+|n−M|≤2^21`, forcing `M∈[n−2^21,n+2^21]` and `β≤1/511`.
proof_steps.statement: Generic adjustment of an absolute raw-bias certificate forces `β≤1/511`.

proof_steps.proof: A useful absolute spectral certificate has `λ<1`, hence the graph is connected. Every edge label is a sum of translated vertex labels, while a path from the root to vertex `i` expresses its translated label as a sum of edge labels. The two spans coincide. Orthogonal decomposition of each sign vector gives the stated mixing bound.
proof_steps.statement: The raw edge-code dimension equals the translated vertex-label span, and its standard certificate is `β=ε²+λ(1−ε²)`.

proof_steps.proof: Integral port multiplicities give `tr(P²)≥m/D`; the spectral bound gives `tr(P²)≤1+(m−1)/511²`. Combining with `mD≤n+2^21` yields `511²m²≤(n+2^21)(m−1+511²)`. Exact evaluation at `m=35000` and monotonicity exclude every larger `m`.
proof_steps.statement: Every target-certifiable template in scope has at most 34,999 vertices.

proof_steps.proof: Fourier orthogonality counts zero-XOR 210-tuples. Restricting to 105 distinct indices used twice gives `Z≥(m−104)^105(209)!!`, and elementary factorial/binomial estimates give `(209)!!>70^105`. The exact endpoint inequalities in the proof yield `Z>2(m²/511)^105` and finally `2^h<2^946`.
proof_steps.statement: The homogeneous edge-label span has dimension at most 945.

proof_steps.proof: Padding preserves raw rank, puncturing cannot increase it, and one all-one row adds at most one dimension.
proof_steps.statement: The final adjusted one-edge code has dimension at most 946 after optional all-one augmentation.

proof_steps.proof: For `t≥3`, rank is at most the number `m≤1024` of seeds. For `t=2`, uniform repetition to length `2^30` is exactly the square of a 32,768-entry repeated seed multiset, so the proved square-convolution ceiling applies.
proof_steps.statement: Uniformly repeated complete Cartesian XOR powers have dimension at most 1025, sharpened to 785 for `t=2`.

research_direction: Expander-walk codes: exact obstruction for ordinary one-edge mixing certificates and complete Cartesian parity clouds.
theorem_statement: Every complete directed-edge XOR lift of an undirected regular rotation multigraph whose target distance is certified only by the standard absolute base-bias/eigenvalue bound `ε²+λ(1−ε²)`, followed by generic padding or puncturing to length `2^30`, has homogeneous dimension at most 945 and dimension at most 946 after one all-one augmentation. Separately, every uniformly repeated complete Cartesian XOR power of arity at least two has dimension at most 1025, with the square case bounded by 785. Hence neither template can improve the proved dimension-1040 endpoint.
title: A 210th-moment ceiling for ordinary one-edge expander certificates
